Meeting 3/2569 · Subcommittee to Study Measures to Oversee Public Ride-Hailing through Applications for Safety and Passenger Protection
Ride-hailing apps: registration, insurance and complaints
se: The meeting considered information from the Department of Land Transport and the Electronic Transactions Development Agency (ETDA). App-based car hire comes under a 2021 ministerial regulation issued under the Motor Vehicle Act 1979. There are 8,740 correctly registered app-based hire cars (Ror Yor 18) and 11,647 public motorcycles serving through apps (Ror Yor 17), 20,387 in all. Reasons some drivers have not registered include hire-purchase fees and interest, higher commercial insurance premiums than for private cars, and the resale price of vehicles with public plates. The Department of Land Transport has worked with the Bank of Thailand and the Office of Insurance Commission (OIC) on hire-purchase contracts and insurance models. The Ministry of Transport has proposed amending the ministerial regulation so that companies can register Ror Yor 18 cars for drivers to rent, and to raise the engine limit for public motorcycles from 125 to 250 cubic centimetres for set models. ETDA said 5 platform operators are linked to the ThaID identity system, and from 1 November 2023 to 30 September 2026 there were 241 complaints, about matters such as job allocation, pay, platform fees and safety. The subcommittee suggested lowering drivers' costs to encourage registration, checking drivers' records and qualifications from time to time, a QR code so passengers can easily check the vehicle and driver, studying extra insurance with platform operators taking part, and looking at the fairness of platform fees (GP). The next meeting will hear about law enforcement, safety, insurance and compensation for accident victims.
it: The situation: 20,387 registered vehicles, and why some drivers have not registered
Solutions: hire-purchase contracts, insurance and amending the ministerial regulation
Oversight of digital platform operators, and 241 complaints
Suggestions such as lowering drivers' costs, QR codes to check vehicles and drivers, and extra insurance

te: Meeting summary video · Ride-hailing apps: registration, insurance and complaints
Setting the scope of the study: safety of ride-hailing cars booked through apps
se: The meeting considered the scope of its study of measures to oversee public ride-hailing vehicles booked through apps, so that services can be checked and followed and passengers are safe throughout the trip. The study covers laws, rules and oversight of platform operators, drivers, vehicles and passengers, focusing on vehicle and driver safety standards, passenger rights, insurance and compensation, responsibility when accidents happen, gaps and overlaps in the law, and data sharing between state agencies and platform operators, leading to policy recommendations. The meeting asked for the plans of the Department of Land Transport and the Electronic Transactions Development Agency (ETDA) to control and follow these services to be presented at the meeting on 29 October 2026.
it: Scope of the study: vehicle and driver safety, passenger protection, insurance and compensation, and gaps in the law
Plans of the Department of Land Transport and ETDA to control and follow the services, for the next meeting
